title: Grothendieck connectedness estimate with a bound on ideal generators
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of finite Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], complete for its maximal-ideal adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $I\subsetneq R$ be an ideal generated by $r\geq0$ elements. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $Y=V(I)$, the closed subset of primes containing $I$. Let $d$ be the minimum dimension of an irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], and let $c$ be the minimum dimension of a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ for which $X\setminus Z$ is not connected. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and connected includes nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme], so $Z=X$ is permitted in the definition of $c$. For every closed subset $T\subseteq Y$, if $\dim T<\min(c,d-1)-r$, then $Y\setminus T$ is nonempty and connected. In particular, if $r<\min(c,d-1)$, then $V(I)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ is nonempty and connected.

proof.text: Put $t=\operatorname{cd}(R,I)$, with local cohomology and its dimension as defined in [lem-per-local-cohomology-generator-bound]. That statement gives $0\leq t\leq r$. We first prove the punctured assertion for the stronger hypothesis $t<\min(c,d-1)$, so that it can later be applied to any proper ideal, including one obtained by adjoining equations.

Under $t<\min(c,d-1)$, the puncture $Y\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ cannot be empty. Otherwise $X\cap V(I)=\{\mathfrak m\}$; [lem-per-isolated-intersection-dimension-bound] with $Z=X$ gives $\dim X\leq t$. Every irreducible component is a subspace of $X$, so its chains are also chains in $X$ and $d\leq\dim X\leq t$, contradicting $t<d-1$. Thus $U\cap Y$ is nonempty, for $U=X\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$.

Still assume $t<\min(c,d-1)$. Since $d>t+1$, apply [lem-per-formal-punctured-idempotent-algebraization] with $A=R$. Its hypotheses are exactly the complete Noetherian local hypotheses of this item. It supplies the ring isomorphism from the colimit of $\Gamma(V_{\rm red},\mathcal O)$ over neighborhoods $V$ of $U\cap Y$ to the inverse limit of $\Gamma(T_n,\mathcal O)$. Here $R_{\rm red}=R/\sqrt{(0)}$ is used only for the structure sheaf: every prime of $R$ contains $\sqrt{(0)}$, and a prime contains $I^n$ exactly when it contains $I$. Thus all $T_n$ have underlying space $U\cap Y$, and $V_{\rm red}$ has the same underlying space as $V$.

If $U\cap Y=W_1\amalg W_2$ were a separation into nonempty clopen subsets, [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent](b) gives on each $T_n$ the idempotent $e_n$ equal to $1$ on $W_1$ and $0$ on $W_2$. Part (c) shows compatibility under reduction, and nonemptiness of both pieces gives $e_n\ne0,1$. Via the preceding isomorphism this compatible family has a preimage $a$ in the colimit ring. Represent $a$ by a section on one $V_{\rm red}$. Since $a^2-a=0$ in the filtered colimit, after restricting to a smaller neighborhood its representative $e$ satisfies $e^2=e$. The neighborhoods form a filtered system because the intersection of two is again a neighborhood. The representative is neither $0$ nor $1$, since either equality would give $e_n=0$ or $1$ for every $n$. By part (b) of the same cited statement it determines a nontrivial clopen separation of $V_{\rm red}$, hence of $V$.

For this disconnected neighborhood $V\subseteq U$ put $Z=X\setminus V$. The inclusion $U\cap Y\subseteq V$ gives $Z\cap Y=\{\mathfrak m\}$. Thus [lem-per-isolated-intersection-dimension-bound] gives $\dim Z\leq t$. The definition of $c$ gives $c\leq\dim Z$, since $X\setminus Z=V$ is disconnected. This contradicts $t<c$. This proves that $Y\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ is nonempty and connected whenever $\operatorname{cd}(R,I)<\min(c,d-1)$.

Now fix closed $T\subseteq Y$. If $T=\varnothing$, then $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ is nonempty and connected: its maximal ideal gives a point, and any clopen piece containing this point contains every prime, because opens are stable under generalization and every prime is contained in the maximal ideal. Hence no separation into two nonempty clopen pieces exists. This proves the assertion in this case without any numerical assumption. Otherwise $T$ contains $\mathfrak m$ (every nonempty closed subset of a local spectrum contains its closed point), and $e=\dim T$ is a finite nonnegative integer. Suppose for contradiction that $Y\setminus T$ is not connected. By [def-weil-connected-scheme], it is either empty or the disjoint union of two nonempty clopen pieces $W_1,W_2$.

Apply [lem-per-prime-avoidance-connectedness-slice] to this nonempty closed $T\subseteq X$. If $Y\setminus T$ is empty use the empty family; otherwise use the two pieces $W_1,W_2$. These are locally closed subsets of $U\setminus T$: $Y\setminus T$ is closed in $U\setminus T$, and each piece is open and closed in it. Obtain $e$ elements $f_i\in\mathfrak m$, and set $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$ and $J=I+K$. The slice $V(K)$ meets $T$ only at $\mathfrak m$ and meets both pieces when present. Since $I$ and all $f_i$ lie in $\mathfrak m$, $J$ is proper.

The puncture $V(J)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ is not connected. Indeed it equals $V(K)\cap(Y\setminus T)$, because $V(K)\cap T=\{\mathfrak m\}$. If $Y=T$ this set is empty. Otherwise its intersections with $W_1$ and $W_2$ are disjoint, nonempty, clopen, and cover it. This supplies the small detail omitted in the source and treats its empty case as well.

For the proper ideal $J=I+(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$, [lem-per-local-cohomology-generator-bound] gives $\operatorname{cd}(R,J)\leq t+e$. Apply the contrapositive of the punctured assertion proved in steps 2--5 to $J$: its disconnected (possibly empty) puncture forces $\min(c,d-1)\leq\operatorname{cd}(R,J)\leq t+e\leq r+e$. Therefore $\dim T=e\geq\min(c,d-1)-r$. This contradicts the hypothesis of the item and proves its general assertion.

Finally $\{\mathfrak m\}\subseteq Y$ is closed and has dimension $0$. If $r<\min(c,d-1)$, then $0<\min(c,d-1)-r$, so the general assertion with $T=\{\mathfrak m\}$ gives the stated nonempty connected puncture.
